# R App Logging {.unnumbered} :::: {.callout-warning collapse='false' appearance='default' icon='false'} ## [Caution]{style='font-weight: bold; font-size: 1.25em;'} ::: {style='font-size: 1.00em; color: #282b2d;'} This section is being revised. Thank you for your patience. ::: :::: This lab covers how to use logging and monitoring to track events inside data science project, and what to do with logs and metrics when they are created. For a refresher, I've included a diagram of the Shiny App and API from the previous lab (i.e., the reactives (user inputs and the **Predict** button), the `httr2` API request/response, and the `plumber` API): ```{=html} ``` ```{mermaid} %%| fig-cap: 'Shiny R App and plumber API' %%| fig-align: center %%{init: {'theme': 'neutral', 'look': 'handDrawn', 'themeVariables': { 'fontFamily': 'monospace'}}}%% graph TD subgraph Inputs["User Inputs"] I1[/"input$bill_length"/] I2[/"input$species"/] I3[/"input$sex"/] I4[/"input$predict"/] end %% Style for inputs %% style I1 fill:#fdd9bb,color:#000,font-size:18px style I2 fill:#fdd9bb,color:#000,font-size:18px style I3 fill:#fdd9bb,color:#000,font-size:18px style I4 fill:#f9a0a0,color:#000,font-size:18px subgraph API["plumber API"] ModBoard("pins::board_folder()") ModPin("vetiver::vetiver_pin_read()") ModRout("plumber::pr()") ModApi("vetiver::vetiver_api()") ApiServ(["Launch

pred()"\] style RenTxt fill:#49297e,color:#fff,font-size:18px style RenPrnt fill:#49297e,color:#fff,font-size:18px ``` ## Packages Below we load the packages for app design (`bslib`, `bsicons`), making the API request (`httr2`), and logging and monitoring (`logger` and `jsonlite`). I chose the [`logger` package](https://daroczig.github.io/logger/index.html) instead of the example from the text ([`log4r`](https://github.com/r-lib/log4r)) because I'm more familiar with it's lightweight and I'm more [familiar with it's features](https://mjfrigaard.github.io/shiny-app-pkgs/logging.html#sec-logging-logger). ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code code-fold="false"} library(shiny) library(bslib) library(bsicons) library(httr2) library(logger) library(jsonlite) ``` ::: ### Configure logging Below we'll configure the log level and assign the [`log_appender()`](https://daroczig.github.io/logger/reference/log_appender.html) with the [`appender_tee()`](https://daroczig.github.io/logger/reference/appender_tee.html).[^app-tee] [^app-tee]: [`appender_tee()`](https://daroczig.github.io/logger/reference/appender_tee.html) determines where the logs will be stored and "*appends log messages to both console and a file*." `logger` also gives us control over the format of the log file with [`log_formatter()`](https://daroczig.github.io/logger/reference/log_formatter.html) (I've found using the [`glue` or `sprintf`](https://daroczig.github.io/logger/reference/formatter_glue_or_sprintf.html) formatter makes the logs more UI friendly). ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code code-fold="false"} logger::log_threshold(level = "DEBUG") logger::log_appender(appender = appender_tee(file = "shiny_app.log")) logger::log_formatter(logger::formatter_glue_or_sprintf) ``` ::: ### App startup Log app startup within observer to access session data (high priority to run early) ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code .code-overflow-wrap code-fold="false"} observe({ logger::log_info("Shiny app started - Session: {session$token} - Host: {session$clientData$url_hostname}") }, priority = 1000) ``` ::: ### User interactions Track user interactions (`throttle` to avoid excessive logging). ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code .code-overflow-wrap code-fold="false"} observe({ logger::log_debug("User input changed - Session: {session$token} - bill_length: {input$bill_length} - species: {input$species} - sex: {input$sex}") }) |> throttle(2000) ``` ::: ### Session token We'll display **Session Token** (a subset of `session$token` as `log_status`) in the upper right-hand corner of the UI. ![](img/lab4-div-session.png){width='100%' fig-align='center'} #### UI A custom `div()` is a good option here (with some minimal styling): ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code .code-overflow-scroll code-fold="false"} div( style = "position: fixed; top: 10px; right: 10px; z-index: 1000; color: #fff;", strong("Session", textOutput("log_status", inline = TRUE)) ) ``` ::: #### Server This output is generated from `substr(session$token, 1, 8)`: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code .code-overflow-wrap code-fold="false"} output$log_status <- renderText({ paste("Token:", substr(session$token, 1, 8)) }) ``` ::: ![](img/lab4-div-session-token.png){width='100%' fig-align='center'} ### Params and Predictions The parameter display and predictions from the API remain largely unchanged here, other than to make room for the **System Status** `column` and `card`. ![](img/lab4-predictions-wireframe.png){width='100%' fig-align='center'} #### UI The params and predictions are displayed in two `bslib::cards()` and include a `value_box()` and `bs_icon()` for the response from the API. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code .code-overflow-scroll code-fold="true" code-summary="show/hide UI Penguin Parameters"} layout_columns( card( card_header("Penguin Parameters"), card_body( verbatimTextOutput(outputId = "vals") ) ), card( card_header("Predicted Mass"), card_body( value_box( showcase_layout = "left center", title = "Grams", value = textOutput(outputId = "pred"), showcase = bs_icon("graph-up"), max_height = "200px", min_height = "200px", ) ) ), col_widths = c(6, 6), row_heights = c(3, 1), ) ``` ::: Note that I've added values for `col_widths` and `row_heights`. #### Server **Reactive values** In the server, we create the reactive `vals()` to be displayed in the **Penguin Parameters** section. I've included warning and error logs for input validation, and a single debugging log to examine the data sent to the API: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code .code-overflow-wrap code-fold="false"} vals <- reactive({ bill_length <- input$bill_length #<1> species <- input$species sex <- input$sex #<1> if (bill_length < 30 || bill_length > 60) { #<2> logger::log_warn("Bill length out of typical range - Session: {session$token} - bill_length: {bill_length}") #<2> } if (is.null(species) || is.null(sex)) { #<3> logger::log_error("Missing required inputs - Session: {session$token} - species_null: {is.null(species)} - sex_null: {is.null(sex)}") return(NULL) } #<3> data <- data.frame( #<4> bill_length_mm = bill_length, species_Chinstrap = as.numeric(species == "Chinstrap"), species_Gentoo = as.numeric(species == "Gentoo"), sex_male = as.numeric(sex == "Male") ) #<4> logger::log_debug("Input data prepared - Session: {session$token} - data: {jsonlite::toJSON(data, auto_unbox = TRUE)}") #<5> return(data) #<6> }) ``` ::: 1. Raw reactive values 2. Logs incorrect input values that can lead to bad predictions or user confusion. 3. Logs critical input validation failures that prevent the application from functioning. 4. Convert reactives into a `data.frame`. 5. Logs formatted input data structure sent to the API. 6. Returns `data.frame` The `vals()` are printed to the UI in a `data.frame`: ![](img/lab4-predictions-vals.png){width='100%' fig-align='center'} **Predictions** I've added logs to the predictions reactive values below. As you can see, the majority of the logs are errors and warning, but I've also included notifications (`showNotification()`) for major events, too. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code .code-overflow-wrap code-fold="false"} pred <- reactive({ request_start <- Sys.time() #<1> request_data <- vals() #<2> if (is.null(request_data)) { logger::log_error("Cannot make prediction with invalid inputs - Session: {session$token}") #<3> return("❌ Invalid inputs") } logger::log_info("Starting prediction request - Session: {session$token} - request_data: {jsonlite::toJSON(request_data, auto_unbox = TRUE)}") #<4> tryCatch({ #<5> showNotification("Predicting penguin mass...", #<6> type = "default", duration = 3) #<6> response <- httr2::request(api_url) |> #<7> httr2::req_method("POST") |> httr2::req_body_json(request_data, auto_unbox = FALSE) |> httr2::req_timeout(30) |> httr2::req_perform() #<7> response_time <- as.numeric(difftime(Sys.time(), request_start, units = "secs")) #<8> response_data <- httr2::resp_body_json(response) #<9> logger::log_info("Prediction successful - Session: {session$token} - response_time_sec: {round(response_time, 3)} - prediction: {response_data$.pred[1]}") #<10> if (response_time > 5) { #<11> logger::log_warn("Slow API response - Session: {session$token} - response_time_sec: {response_time}") } #<11> showNotification("✅ Prediction successful!", #<12> type = "message", duration = 3) #<12> return(response_data$.pred[1]) #<13> }, error = function(e) { error_msg <- conditionMessage(e) # <14> response_time <- as.numeric(difftime(Sys.time(), request_start, units = "secs")) #<15> logger::log_error("Prediction request failed - Session: {session$token} - error: {error_msg} - response_time_sec: {round(response_time, 3)}") #<16> if (grepl("Connection refused|couldn't connect", error_msg, ignore.case = TRUE)) { #<17> user_msg <- "API not available - is the server running on port 8080?" logger::log_error("API connection refused - Session: {session$token}") #<17> } else if (grepl("timeout|timed out", error_msg, ignore.case = TRUE)) { #<18> user_msg <- "Request timed out - API may be overloaded" logger::log_warn("API timeout occurred - Session: {session$token}") #<18> } else { user_msg <- paste("API Error:", substr(error_msg, 1, 50)) logger::log_error("Unknown API error - Session: {session$token} - error: {error_msg}") #<19> } showNotification(paste("❌", user_msg), type = "error", duration = 5) #<20> return(paste("❌", user_msg)) }) #<5> }) |> bindEvent(input$predict, ignoreInit = TRUE) #<21> ``` ::: 1. Record API request start time 2. Reactive values from UI 3. Logs when/if the prediction requests fail because of data validation issues (critical application logic problems). 4. Logs initiation of prediction request w/ input parameters for request tracing and/or debugging. 5. Handles all possible API communication failures (i.e., network issues, timeouts, etc) and provides meaningful error messages to users instead of crashing the application. 6. Notification for predicting penguin mass 7. `httr2` API request 8. Record API response time 9. API prediction response data 10. Logs successful predictions and performance metrics/results 11. Logs performance issues that could impact user experience and/or indicate need for system optimization. 12. Notification for successful prediction 13. Prediction values 14. `tryCatch()` error message 15. API Response time 16. Logs complete prediction failures with diagnostic information for troubleshooting critical application functionality. 17. Logs when the API is unreachable, indicating critical system failure. 18. Logs API timeout events that suggest network issues or API overload. 19. Logs unexpected API errors that don't match known failure patterns. 20. Notification for error 21. Trigger when Predict button is clicked. After clicking **Predict**, the response from the API displays the predicted penguin mass in grams: ![](img/lab4-predictions-pred.png){width='100%' fig-align='center'} ### System Status In the **System Status** display, we'll 1) send a `ping` to the API and return the result as **API Status**, 2) print a subset of **Recent Logs** from the log file specified above in the `logger::log_appender()` function, and 3) include a timestamp displaying when the log file was **Last updated**. ![](img/lab4-system-status-wireframe.png){width='100%' fig-align='center'} #### UI We can make room for a **System Status** section in the UI as a `card()` using `layout_columns()` (as long as we set the `col_widths` and a fixed `height`). The `div()` for the logs also gets some custom styling: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code .code-overflow-wrap code-fold="false"} layout_columns( card( card_header("System Status"), card_body( h5("API Status:"), #<1> textOutput("api_health"),#<1> h5("Recent Logs:"),#<2> div( style = "font-family: 'Ubuntu Mono', monospace; font-size: 13px; background-color: #f8f9fa; padding: 10px; border-radius: 5px;", verbatimTextOutput("recent_logs", placeholder = TRUE) ),#<2> h6("Last updated:", #<3> textOutput("log_timestamp", inline = TRUE) ), style = "max-height: 350px; overflow-y: auto;" #<3> ) ), col_widths = c(12), #<4> height = "300px" #<5> ) ``` ::: 1. Results from `ping` sent to API 2. Log display from `shiny_log.log` file 3. Last modification time of `shiny_log.log` file 4. Full width 5. Fixed height We'll cover how to include each output in the **System Status** below. #### API Status The status of the `ping` sent to the API can return one of three results: `✅ API Online` (response = 200), `⚠️ API Issues` (non-200 status), `❌ API Offline` (non-response). ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code .code-overflow-wrap code-fold="false"} api_health <- reactive({ tryCatch({ logger::log_debug("Checking API health - Session: {session$token}") #<1> response <- httr2::request("http://127.0.0.1:8080/ping") |> #<2> httr2::req_timeout(5) |> httr2::req_perform() #<2> if (httr2::resp_status(response) == 200) { #<3> logger::log_info("API health check successful - Session: {session$token}") return("✅ API Online") #<3> } else { logger::log_warn("API health check returned non-200 status - Session: {session$token} - status: {httr2::resp_status(response)}") #<4> return("⚠️ API Issues") #<4> } }, error = function(e) { #<5> logger::log_error("API health check failed - Session: {session$token} - error: {conditionMessage(e)}") return("❌ API Offline") #<5> }) }) ``` ::: 1. Logs when health checks are initiated to track frequency and timing. 2. `ping` sent to API 3. Logs the external API is responding normally. 4. Logs to API degradation or partial failures that may impact user experience. 5. Logs complete API connectivity failures that render the application non-functional. :::{layout="[35,65]" layout-valign="top"} When we initially launch, we see the offline status is accurate (the API isn't running): ![](img/lab4-api-health-check-offline.png){width='100%' fig-align='center'} When we run the API, we can see the `ping` responds with an online status: ![](img/lab4-api-health-check-online.png){width='100%' fig-align='center'} ::: #### Recent Logs All the events captured with `logger::log_*()` functions are written to the log file (`shiny_log.log`). To display the most recent logs in the UI, we can use Shiny's [`reactiveFileReader()`](https://shiny.posit.co/r/reference/shiny/latest/reactivefilereader.html) and configure it to poll our log file every 1 second (1000ms) for changes: ```{mermaid} %%| fig-cap: 'Logging in Server' %%| fig-align: center %%| fig-width: 7.0 %%{init: {'theme': 'neutral', 'look': 'handDrawn', 'themeVariables': { 'fontFamily': 'monospace'}}}%% flowchart TD subgraph User["Log Generation"] Q(["User
inputs"]) R(["API
calls"]) S(["System
events"]) %% T@{ shape: rect, label: "logger::log_*
functions" } T["logger::log_*
functions"] end Q --> T R --> T S --> T T -- "Written to"--> A subgraph FileSys["File System"] %% A@{ shape: lin-doc, label: "shiny_app.log" } A[\"Log file: shiny_app.log"\] A1("Modification
Time") A2("File
Contents") end A --> A1 & A2 A -."changes trigger".-> B subgraph ReactFile["Reactive File"] %% B@{ shape: subproc, label: "reactiveFileReader()" } B{{"reactiveFileReader() "}} C{"Log file
exists?"} D("lines
last_mod
total_lines") E("lines:character(0)
last_mod:Sys.time()
total_lines:0") end B --"checks every 1 second"--> C C -- Yes (returns list)--> D C -- No (returns empty list)--> E style Q fill:#FFF,color:#000,rx:20,ry:20,font-size:18px style R fill:#FFF,color:#000,rx:20,ry:20,font-size:18px style S fill:#FFF,color:#000,rx:20,ry:20,font-size:18px style T fill:#4ac590,color:#000,rx:20,ry:20,font-size:18px style A fill:#FFF,color:#000,rx:20,ry:20,font-size:18px style A1 fill:#62d3fc,color:#000,rx:12,ry:12,font-size:18px style A2 fill:#62d3fc,color:#000,rx:12,ry:12,font-size:18px style B fill:#d08300,stroke:#d08300,color:#fff,rx:12,ry:12,font-size:18px style C fill:#f2b857,stroke:#000,color:#000,font-size:18px style D fill:#f2b857,stroke:#000,color:#000,rx:20,ry:20,font-size:18px style E fill:#f2b857,stroke:#000,color:#000,rx:20,ry:20,font-size:18px ``` The reactive returned from `reactiveFileReader()` will contain a list with the log line (`lines`), the time this file was last modified (`last_mod`), and a count of the total number of lines in the log file (`total_lines`). ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code .code-overflow-wrap code-fold="false"} log_file_content <- reactiveFileReader( intervalMillis = 1000, session = session, filePath = "shiny_app.log", readFunc = function(filePath) { if (file.exists(filePath)) { #<1> lines <- readLines(filePath, warn = FALSE) mod_time <- file.mtime(filePath) #<1> list( #<2> lines = lines, last_mod = mod_time, total_lines = length(lines) ) #<2> } else { list( #<3> lines = character(0), last_mod = Sys.time(), total_lines = 0 ) #<3> } } ) ``` ::: 1. Read all lines and get file modification time. 2. Return both content and timestamp. 3. Return empty list. To make this display more manageable, we'll limit the number of extracted logs to the five most recent lines (unless there are less than five total lines in the log file). We'll also format the logs to be displayed in the `verbatimTextOutput()` and include a message if the log file is empty. ```{mermaid} %%| fig-cap: 'Displaying logs' %%| fig-align: center %%| fig-width: 7.0 %%{init: {'theme': 'neutral', 'look': 'handDrawn', 'themeVariables': { 'fontFamily': 'monospace'}}}%% flowchart TD A{{"reactiveFileReader() "}} subgraph LogProc["Log Processing"] H(["Reads shiny_app.log"]) I{"More than 5 lines in total_lines?"} J("Print last 5 lines") K("Print all lines") L["Format: paste(lines,
collapse = '\\n')"] M["Return:
'No logs available'"] end A --> H H --> I I -- "Yes J I -- "No" --> K J --> L K --> L H -- "No lines"--> M subgraph UI["UI Rendering"] N[/"log_file_content()"/] subgraph P["Display in div"] O["verbatimTextOutput(recent_logs)"] end end L & M --> N N --> P style A fill:#d08300,stroke:#d08300,color:#ffffff,rx:12,ry:12,text-align:center style H fill:#216654,stroke:#216654,color:#ffffff,rx:12,ry:12,text-align:center style L fill:#40915d,stroke:#216654,color:#ffffff,rx:12,ry:12 style M fill:#40915d,stroke:#216654,color:#ffffff,rx:12,ry:12 style N fill:#772f98,color:#fff,text-align:center style O fill:#cc66d3,color:000,text-align:center ``` ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code .code-overflow-wrap code-fold="false"} output$recent_logs <- renderText({ log_data <- log_file_content() if (length(log_data$lines) > 0) { #<1> recent_lines <- if (log_data$total_lines > 5) { tail(log_data$lines, 5) } else { log_data$lines } #<1> logger::log_debug("Updating recent logs display - Session: {session$token} - showing {length(recent_lines)} lines") #<2> paste(recent_lines, collapse = "\n") #<3> } else { "No logs available" } }) ``` ::: 1. Get last 5 lines of log file or complete log file 2. Log that we're updating the display (at `DEBUG` level to avoid spam) 3. Format the recent logs before displaying in the UI. If the API is running, the log file will contain the status of the health check and the app start-up/initialization message: ```{.default} INFO [2025-09-09 13:22:10] Shiny app started - Session: 8f018f03ac7f1339dc2f826077156264 - Host: localhost INFO [2025-09-09 13:22:10] API health check successful - Session: 8f018f03ac7f1339dc2f826077156264 INFO [2025-09-09 13:27:40] Shiny application initialized - timestamp: 2025-09-09 13:27:40.00443 - r_version: R version 4.5.1 (2025-06-13) INFO [2025-09-09 13:27:41] Shiny app started - Session: 40ba19c3b213c5aa6c8589dc15aa4bd8 - Host: localhost INFO [2025-09-09 13:27:41] API health check successful - Session: 40ba19c3b213c5aa6c8589dc15aa4bd8 ``` We can these logs show up in the UI: ![](img/lab4-api-recent-logs-display.png){width='100%' fig-align='center'} When a user clicks on **Predict**, the values are sent in a request to the API, a response is returned, and the log file is updated with: ```{.default} INFO [2025-09-09 13:37:54] Starting prediction request - Session: 40ba19c3b213c5aa6c8589dc15aa4bd8 - request_data: [{"bill_length_mm":45,"species_Chinstrap":0,"species_Gentoo":0,"sex_male":1}] INFO [2025-09-09 13:37:55] Prediction successful - Session: 40ba19c3b213c5aa6c8589dc15aa4bd8 - response_time_sec: 0.619 - prediction: 4180.7965 INFO [2025-09-09 13:37:55] Displaying prediction to user - Session: 40ba19c3b213c5aa6c8589dc15aa4bd8 - display_value: 4180.8 grams ``` We can also see out UI updates with the recent logs: ![](img/lab4-api-recent-logs-predictions.png){width='100%' fig-align='center'} Finally, we should see the log file included in our Shiny app directory: ```{.default} ├── app.R ├── R.Rproj ├── README.md ├── renv ├── renv.lock └── shiny_app.log #<1> 2 directories, 5 files ``` 1. New log file! #### Last updated The final **Last updated** section includes the time and date the `log_file_content()` reactive was last updated. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code .code-overflow-wrap code-fold="false"} output$log_timestamp <- renderText({ log_data <- log_file_content() format(log_data$last_mod, "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S") }) ``` ::: ![Click on image to enlarge](img/lab4-last-updated.png){width='100%' fig-align='center'}
